chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qarawī, from Abān, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I recite two surahs in one rakʿah? He said: Yes. I said: Is it not said, “Give every surah its due of bowing and prostration”? He said: That is in the obligatory prayer; but as for the supererogatory prayer, there is no harm in it.

key_terms.بَأْسٌ: harm or objection in legal context

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite two surahs in one rakʿah of prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on reciting two surahs in a single rakʿah. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام clarifies that the discouragement applies to the obligatory prayer, whereas in the supererogatory prayer there is no problem with combining two surahs in one rakʿah.
